Calculate rest disparity between home and away teams

Source: R/rest.R
calculate_rest_disparity.Rd

Computes each team's days of rest entering every game from gameday, then derives the rest disparity, short-week flags, and off-bye flags. Rest is computed within a season, so the first game of each team's season has NA rest (nflverse reports 7 for season openers).

Usage

calculate_rest_disparity(schedule, short_week_days = 6, bye_rest_days = 13)

Arguments

schedule

A data frame with game_id, gameday, home_team, and away_team. season is used for grouping when present.

short_week_days

Rest below this many days is flagged as a short week. Defaults to 6, which catches the 4-5 day Thursday turnarounds.

bye_rest_days

Rest at or above this many days is flagged as coming off a bye. Defaults to 13, the shortest realistic post-bye rest.

Value

schedule with gameday coerced to Date, plus home_rest_days, away_rest_days, rest_disparity, home_short_week, away_short_week, home_off_bye, and away_off_bye. Positive rest_disparity means the home team is better rested.

Examples

games <- subset(nfl_schedules_sample, home_team == "KC" | away_team == "KC")
rest <- calculate_rest_disparity(games)
head(rest[, c("game_id", "home_rest_days", "away_rest_days", "rest_disparity")])
#> # A tibble: 6 x 4
#>   game_id        home_rest_days away_rest_days rest_disparity
#>   <chr>                   <dbl>          <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1 2024_01_BAL_KC             NA             NA             NA
#> 2 2024_02_CIN_KC             10             NA             NA
#> 3 2024_03_KC_ATL             NA              7             NA
#> 4 2024_04_KC_LAC             NA              7             NA
#> 5 2024_05_NO_KC               8             NA             NA
#> 6 2024_07_KC_SF              NA             13             NA
